sec: Calcium distribution, corrected calcium and absorption · p874

items.q: Total body calcium (1000–1300 g) resides in bones to the extent of:
Match the soft-tissue calcium fractions — 1) Free (ionized)  2) Bound to albumin  3) Bound to other proteins … A) 40%  B) 12%  C) 48%
items.exp: Soft-tissue calcium: 48% free ionized, 40% albumin-bound, 12% other proteins. (Book p874)

items.q: The normal corrected calcium range is:

items.exp: Corrected Ca = Total Ca + 0.8 (4 − albumin level). (Book p874)

items.q: Corrected calcium defines hypocalcaemia below and hypercalcaemia above:
Free ionized calcium functions include sensitizing CaSR, myocyte contractility, neuromuscular activity and:
items.exp: Functions: sensitize CaSR, myocyte contractility, neuromuscular activity, bone mineralization. (Book p874)

items.q: ‘In acidosis, H+ competes with calcium for albumin, raising the free Ca2+.’
items.exp: ↑ H+ (acidosis) → ↑ free Ca2+; ↓ pH by 0.1 unit → ↑ Ca2+ by 0.1 meq/L. (Book p874)

items.q: A fall in pH by 0.1 unit raises ionized calcium by:

opts: Free Ca2+ plus Ca2+ complexed to anions
items.exp: Plasma Ca = free Ca2+ + Ca2+ complexed to anions. (Book p874)

items.q: Calcium absorption occurs in the proximal small intestine with the order:
items.exp: Site: proximal small intestine (jejunum > duodenum); ~20% net absorption (~200 mg), enhanced by acid. (Book p874)

items.q: Match absorption route — 1) 95% active transcellular  2) 5% passive paracellular … A) Independent of calcitriol  B) Tightly controlled by calcitriol
Calcitriol drives transcellular calcium absorption by:
opts: Binding nuclear receptors → releasing calbindin → activating TRPV5/6; exit via Ca2+ ATPase
items.exp: Calcitriol binds nuclear receptors, releases calbindin, activates TRPV5/6; calcium exits via Ca2+ ATPase. (Book p874)

items.q: Free ionized calcium functions listed are sensitizing CaSR, myocyte contractility, neuromuscular activity and bone mineralization. Pick the ODD ONE OUT:
items.exp: Ionized Ca sensitizes CaSR and drives contractility, neuromuscular activity and mineralization — suppression is the odd one. (Book p874)

items.q: A patient's ABG shows pH 7.25. The expected effect on serum calcium is:
opts: Acidosis raises free ionized Ca2+ as H+ competes with Ca2+ for albumin
Acidosis lowers free ionized Ca2+ by albumin binding
No change in the ionized fraction
items.exp: H+ competes for albumin: acidosis increases free Ca; ↓pH 0.1 → ↑Ca 0.1 meq/L. (Book p874)
